module purpose: neorv32_twd is a bus-programmable two-wire device interface. It stores control settings from bus writes, queues outgoing bytes in a TX FIFO, samples twd_sda_i/twd_scl_i to detect bus events and shift address/data bytes, returns control/status or RX data on the bus response, drives twd_sda_o, exports clkgen_en_o, and raises irq_o.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into stored control fields
one-cycle RX/TX FIFO clear requests written via control bits
a detected start condition begins or restarts the serial bus engine
sampled serial input is qualified into edges/start/stop and shifted into the engine byte register for address matching and RX-byte capture
an outgoing response byte is selected from TX FIFO data, the backed-up byte, or all ones and is driven serially on twd_sda_o
interrupt request and busy/status information produced from control and FIFO/engine state
stored control/status fields or an RX byte returned on bus reads
external reset clears control, backup, sample, engine and output state to known defaults

conceptual assets.concept: Controller enable setting that turns the interface on and off
conceptual assets.reasoning: The stored enable bit is written at line 159, read back at line 172, copied to clkgen_en_o at line 198, and it directly gates FIFO clearing (lines 230 and 281), interrupt generation (line 293), sample qualification (line 315), and engine state progression (lines 381, 389, 397, 421, 434 and 465). If corrupted, the module would operate, stop, or clear queues incorrectly. Availability is also established because the bit is held between writes and exported on clkgen_en_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Explicit RX and TX FIFO clear requests
conceptual assets.reasoning: The clear-request bits are written at lines 160 and 161, forced back to '0' by default at lines 154 and 155, and each drives a FIFO clear input through lines 281 and 230. A wrong pulse would erase queued bytes or fail to clear them when requested, so the configure flow depends on their exact value. Availability is established as a one-cycle stored request that reaches the FIFO clear control.

conceptual assets.concept: Sampling-clock source selection for serial input qualification
conceptual assets.reasoning: The stored selection bit is written at line 162, read back at line 173, and selects which clkgen_i bit becomes smp.clk_en at line 329; smp.clk_en then controls when the sampled serial histories advance at lines 316 to 319. If corrupted, start/stop and edge detection would be performed at the wrong cadence, so the operate flow depends on its integrity. Availability is established because the bit is held between writes and consumed by the sampling logic.

conceptual assets.concept: Configured 7-bit address that must match the captured serial address before a response is issued
conceptual assets.reasoning: The 7-bit value is written at line 163, read back at line 174, and compared against engine.sreg(7 downto 1) at line 402 before the engine can move to S_RESP at line 406; otherwise it stays out of the response path. If corrupted, the module would accept or ignore the wrong serial address. Availability is established because the stored value is preserved between writes and used by the address-match decision.

conceptual assets.concept: Stored interrupt-condition mask bits that decide which FIFO status conditions can raise an interrupt
conceptual assets.reasoning: Three control bits are written at lines 164 to 166, read back at lines 175 to 177, and used in the irq_o expression at lines 293 to 296: they qualify whether RX available, RX not-free, and TX not-available participate in the interrupt decision. If corrupted, the module would report the wrong interrupt conditions. Availability is established because the bits are held between writes and consumed continuously by irq generation.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt request event exported on irq_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_o is registered from the enabled interrupt expression at lines 293 to 296 and cleared on reset at line 291. The report flow depends on irq_o reflecting exactly the enabled FIFO-status conditions, so corruption would deliver a wrong interrupt event to the external consumer. Availability is established because the event is produced on clock edges when the visible conditions hold.

conceptual assets.concept: Stored policy bit that selects the backed-up TX byte instead of all ones when no TX FIFO byte is available
conceptual assets.reasoning: The policy bit is written at line 167, read back at line 178, and it gates the engine.rdata mux at lines 250 to 252: when tx_fifo.avail is not asserted, the bit decides whether engine.rdata takes tx_dummy or (others => '1'). If corrupted, the serial response path would source the wrong fallback value. Availability is established because the bit is held and used whenever the no-data condition occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Stored policy bit that suppresses the response path for a matched command when the line-403 condition holds
conceptual assets.reasoning: The policy bit is written at line 168, read back at line 179, and participates in the address-phase decision at lines 403 to 406: when engine.sreg(0) = '1' and tx_fifo.free = '0', the bit decides whether the engine returns to S_IDLE instead of entering S_RESP. If corrupted, the module would expose or suppress responses contrary to the implemented condition. Availability is established because the stored bit is preserved and consumed by the state-transition logic.

conceptual assets.concept: Qualified serial-bus event decisions derived from sampled SDA/SCL history
conceptual assets.reasoning: smp.clk_en is computed at line 329, the external serial inputs are captured into sample histories at lines 311 to 319, and bus_event derives smp.scl_rise, smp.scl_fall, smp.start and smp.stop at lines 344 to 347. The engine then uses those decisions for start/restart, stop handling, shifting, acknowledge capture, and byte completion at lines 381, 389, 397, 399, 401, 411, 423, 427, 434, 436, 438, 448, 455, 467, 473 and 477. If these event decisions are corrupted, transaction sequencing and byte timing become incorrect. Availability is established when sampling is enabled and smp.clk_en advances the histories.

conceptual assets.concept: Captured serial address/data byte held in the engine shift register
conceptual assets.reasoning: The incoming serial bit stream is shifted into engine.sreg on qualified clock rises at lines 412 and 449. That stored byte is then used for address matching at line 402, its low bit is captured into engine.cmd at line 420, and it is handed toward the RX FIFO through lines 282 and 283 when engine.wr_we is asserted at line 443. If corrupted, the module would match the wrong address, decode the wrong command bit, or enqueue the wrong received byte. Availability is established because the register accumulates bits across successive qualified clock rises.

engine.state is the central stored phase variable selected by the case statement at line 377 and updated by the transitions at lines 382, 390, 392, 398, 400, 404, 406, 422, 424, 435, 437, 441, 444, 466 and 469. engine.cmd captures engine.sreg(0) at line 420 and then decides receive/transmit behavior at lines 443, 453, 468 and 477. engine.ack captures smp.sda at line 474 and decides whether the ACK phase returns to S_RTX at lines 468 to 469. engine.busy reports idle versus non-idle at line 494 and is read out at line 188. Corrupting these stored decisions changes the implemented sequencing, transfer direction, continuation/termination behavior, and reported busy status. Availability is established because they are held across cycles and updated only under the visible event conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Outgoing serial response data driven on twd_sda_o in transmit mode
conceptual assets.reasoning: tx_dummy stores the backed-up byte at lines 241 to 244, engine.rdata selects the response source at lines 250 to 252, engine.sreg and engine.dout load that response data at lines 428 to 429 and 463 to 464, and twd_sda_o copies engine.dout at line 454 when engine.cmd = '1'. The operate flow therefore depends on the exact selected byte and bit values being preserved and driven out; corruption would make the external consumer receive the wrong serial response. Availability is established when the engine enters the response/transmit path and the selected value is loaded and shifted out.
